simple.meaning: עָשׁוּק (ʻâshûwq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “used in plural masculine as abstractly, tyranny.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Job, Ecclesiastes, Amos, beginning at Job 35:9. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָשׁוּק (H6217) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עָשׁוּק (ʻâshûwq) / H6217 is traced through Job 35:9, Ecclesiastes 4:1, Amos 3:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.
